A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FocalPO and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across the expanded appendix structure.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-optimization experiments on two model families, benchmark results in Table 1, a weighting comparison, and generated-response examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports Arena-Hard evaluations and additional downstream task results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The implemented FocalPO objective in Eq. 4, preference-probability parameterization, and reference-model formulation remain unchanged. The revised gamma selection concerns experimental settings; the added mathematical appendices do not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Arena-Hard replaces MT-Bench, while Alpaca Eval and both preference-training datasets remain. Appendix D adds HellaSwag, ARC, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, GSM8K, and MMLU evaluations, substantially extending coverage to commonsense reasoning, science questions, truthfulness, coreference, mathematics, and knowledge.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DPO, ORPO, KTO, and SimPO as comparators. The new downstream Table 2 evaluates these methods and additionally includes SFT as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 replaces MT-Bench average scoring with Arena-Hard pairwise win rates, using 500 prompts and specified reference and judge models. Appendix D introduces OpenLLM evaluation. Gamma changes from searching [0.05, 0.07] to fixing 0.05; the reported Mistral setting changes from 0.07 to 0.05. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not confirmation that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The correct-versus-incorrect weighting comparison in Figures 1 and 4 and the walking-around-the-world case study are retained. Appendix D adds downstream benchmark comparisons, without a separate new ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error-analysis experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Arena-Hard entries replace MT-Bench results; FocalPO reports win rates of 34.6 for Llama-3 and 17.1 for Mistral. New Table 2 supplies six downstream task scores and reported averages for each method/model combination. Mistral SimPO's Alpaca Eval LCWR changes from 21.5 to 17.0. These include new benchmark results, not cross-version performance gains under identical conditions.

T1.justification: New Appendix A introduces Lemma 1 and a proof bounding FocalPO loss by a gamma-weighted combination of preference entropy and DPO loss for gamma in [0, 1]. Appendix B adds an explicit derivation of the existing FocalPO gradient. These formal arguments are absent from v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion newly emphasize performance with the introduced hyperparameter fixed, and the empirical claim now includes Arena-Hard instead of MT-Bench. The central contribution—improving preference optimization by emphasizing correctly ranked pairs—remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds an entropy-based interpretation involving reduced overconfidence and applicability outside the training distribution. Appendix D interprets downstream capability trade-offs through the alignment-tax perspective. The limitations now discuss fixed gamma and speculate that further tuning could improve results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a FocalPO code-access link, explicitly identifies the Alpaca Eval judge, and names the OpenLLM evaluation implementation. Training documentation revises gamma and removes the Llama-3 DPO checkpoint link. Hardware, training libraries, and most implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Arena-Hard, OpenLLM evaluation, downstream datasets, and alignment-tax discussion, while removing the MT-Bench reference. The retained related-work section preserves FocalPO's positioning relative to DPO, SimPO, ODPO, KTO, and ORPO.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most existing prose are retained. Local edits compress contribution bullets into numbered prose, clarify the loss-approximation wording and gamma notation, and update appendix organization and cross-references around the new material.

P2.justification: v2 adds downstream Table 2, revises Table 1's benchmark headers and caption, and corrects its Mistral win-rate winner highlighting. Figure 4 moves between columns, and appendix prose changes to a single-column layout. All four plot images and the qualitative response tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Broader evaluations and added code-access information offer useful gains, but the additions introduce unresolved reliability problems. Table 2's displayed Llama-3 SFT scores average 64.3, whereas it reports 68.3 without explaining another aggregation rule. Appendix B Eq. 11 also omits the negative sign required by Eq. 4. These reporting and derivation problems undermine the added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
